title: Generalized Binomial Coefficients and Extended Identities

problemStatement.formal: \text{Prove the key binomial identities: Vandermonde, Hockey Stick, Product Identity, and bounds.}
problemStatement.plain: Extend the combinations formula with core identities: Vandermonde's convolution C(m+n,r) = Σ C(m,k)C(n,r-k), Hockey Stick Σ C(i+r,r) = C(n+r+1,r+1), Product identity C(n,k)C(k,j) = C(n,j)C(n-j,k-j), and bounds C(n,k) ≤ 2^n and C(2n,n) ≤ 4^n.
whyMatters: Vandermonde's identity is fundamental for counting arguments and generating functions
Hockey stick identity enables telescoping sums in combinatorial proofs
Product identity is used in probability and double counting arguments
Central binomial bound C(2n,n) ≤ 4^n is key in Erdős's proof of Bertrand's postulate

proven: Vandermonde's Identity: C(m+n, r) = Σ_{k=0}^{r} C(m,k) * C(n,r-k) (Lean proof, 0 sorries)
Hockey Stick Identity: Σ_{i=0}^{n} C(i+r,r) = C(n+r+1,r+1) (Lean proof, 0 sorries)
Product Identity: C(n,k)*C(k,j) = C(n,j)*C(n-j,k-j) for j≤k≤n (Lean proof, 0 sorries)
Alternating Row Sum: Σ (-1)^k C(n,k) = 0 for n≥1 (Int.alternating_sum_range_choose_of_ne)
Central Binomial Bound: C(2n,n) ≤ 4^n (proved, key for Bertrand's postulate)
open: Newton's generalized binomial theorem: (1+x)^α = Σ C(α,k)x^k for non-integer α (partial Mathlib coverage)
q-analog of binomial coefficients for quantum groups
knownResults.goal: Prove and formalize the core extended binomial identities.

currentState.focus: Formalization complete from PR #2980 — 0 sorries, all core identities proved

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: CombinationsFormulaOQ01.lean has 0 sorries (PR #2980). All core identities proved: Vandermonde (via Nat.add_choose_eq), Hockey Stick (by induction using Nat.choose_succ_succ), Product Identity (factorial cancellation), Row/Alternating sums from Mathlib, and bounds C(n,k)≤2^n, C(2n,n)≤4^n.
builtItems: Concrete Fibonacci connection via Pascal diagonal sums (verified examples)
insights: Hockey Stick proved by induction using Nat.choose_succ_succ as the Pascal step
Product Identity proved via factorial cancellation: multiply both sides by j!(k-j)!(n-k)! and show both = n!
Nat.choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial is the key Mathlib lemma: C(a,b) * b! * (a-b)! = a!
C(n,k) ≤ 2^n: single term is bounded by the full row sum (Finset.single_le_sum)
C(2n,n) ≤ 4^n chains through choose_le_pow2 and pow_mul
Fibonacci connection: diagonal sums Σ C(n-j,j) = F(n+1) — verified for small cases
The file provides concrete native_decide verifications for all identities
mathlibGaps: Newton's generalized binomial theorem for non-integer α not in base Mathlib
q-analogs of binomial coefficients not in Mathlib
nextSteps: Could extend to generalized binomial coefficients C(α,k) for real/complex α using Mathlib's Complex.choose or Pochhammer symbols
Could formalize Zhu-Vandermonde identity (generalization to non-integers)
